text.p: Comments by three economists on Sweden's state budget announced on Friday.
Carl B. Hamilton, Chief Economist, Svenska Handelsbanken:

"In the long run there is a good improvement of public finances but this points to volatile public finance. As the finance minister said public finances are very sensitive to business fluctuation, so if we have a downturn in a few years' time we are uncertain how the budget deficit will behave in such a situation but for the next two years the situation looks promising.

The combination of the statements about stability of ERM point today to a more decisive will to enter ERM and a more favourable look upon future membership of EMU. This is an interesting fine tuning change in attitude." he added.

"We are less concerned about volatile public finances. We have found that the sensitivity of the budget to the economic cycle has decreased. I agree that the unemployment isssue is a question mark. There's a shift toward being more positive towards ERM and EMU. The Swedish crown has good value."
"Even if we get a growth of three percent I think it will be difficult to halve unemployment. One can see in the figures that state finances have improved, promises have been kept," he added.
I think that it (ERM) could be on the agenda in 1997 after parliament has made a decision on EMU."
